sections.heading: The streams and what they are
sections.body:
1. Six streams, 4,860 tons a year, all understood on released results; three carry QR-14 (destruction with a certificate) and the solvent carries 3.2% halogens the profile did not say.
The process water is not ignitable and carries 40 mg/L of active ingredient, so aqueous treatment is not an outlet; the solvent cannot go to Fox Hollow fuel blending; the product-contact solids are Texas state-regulated and QR-14 rules out landfill for them.

3. Every stream has a permitted unit with capacity; Port Terrell is 94% booked with no first-quarter plan and its kiln down, so Granger carries the QR-14 streams with about 2,175 tons of first-quarter headroom.
Granger is 70.9% booked for the fourth quarter; Port Terrell's first quarter, if it repeats the fourth, has about 630 tons of headroom against 725 tons of process water a quarter. The committee ruled out new pharmaceutical volume on Port Terrell until its plan is published. Tidewater is under renewal; aerosols fit at Cypress Landing; the scrubber water at Bayou Verde.

sections.heading: Options considered
sections.body:
Quote the QR-14 streams on Port Terrell with Granger as the fallback, capacity to be confirmed before signature (preferred)
Process water, solvent and product-contact solids incinerated at Port Terrell at the book; lab packs at Granger; aerosols at Cypress Landing; scrubber water to Bayou Verde deep well. Granger named as the fallback in the schedule; Port Terrell's first-quarter plan confirmed before the contract is signed.
Quote a year: $3.56M · Margin: $1.53M · 43.0% · Capacity: not confirmed · Approval: VP Sales and Director
Trade-off: Earns $0.29M a year more than Granger, on a unit that is 94% booked, has no first-quarter plan and is down today; if the plan shows no room the quote moves to Granger at 34.7%.

Quote on Granger for the QR-14 streams, Port Terrell as the alternative
The same quote with the three QR-14 streams at Granger, the capacity in the bookings and the longer haul.
Quote a year: $3.56M · Margin: $1.24M · 34.7% · Capacity: in the bookings · Committee: as decided
Trade-off: Gives up $0.29M a year of margin for capacity that is in the bookings.

Decline the process water and quote the other five streams
Quote the solvent, the expired product, the aerosols, the product-contact solids and the scrubber water, and tell Halden the process water needs capacity we cannot show until Port Terrell publishes its plan.
Quote a year: $1.41M · Margin: $0.46M · 32.9% · Anchor stream: lost · One vendor: not met
Trade-off: Avoids the haul and the capacity question, but gives up $2.15M a year of revenue and the stream Halden cares about most; they asked for one vendor.

fromGoal.title: Every accepted stream has an outlet with capacity and stays above the floor: check every nightly load

sections.heading: What we ask, and by when
sections.body:
Confirm the Granger slots, book the trucks and hold the two loads so every stranded shipment has an outlet before its clock runs out.

Goal: Keep every accepted stream with a permitted outlet that has capacity when it arrives, and every stream above the margin floor, across the 13 facilities and the third-party outlets. Check each nightly load of profiles, manifests, bookings, outlet approvals and the price book; when a shipment loses its outlet, an approval runs out or a stream falls under the floor, size it, look at what the rest of the network can take, and come back with what can still be done.
Decision asked: Confirm the re-routes, the holds and the outlet loads so every stranded shipment has an outlet inside its clock, and bill the fee on the streams under the floor
Deadline: Granger slots confirmed before the trucks are booked on Wednesday 4 November at noon; the first clock runs out on 11 November; the kiln is back on feed on 15 November

sections.heading: The shipments and their exposure
sections.body:
1. Eighteen positions need a decision: fourteen shipments (911 tons, $0.71M) booked for Port Terrell units that are down, two approvals that expire, two streams under the floor.
Six of the shipments are on the pad at Galena Shores with the first clock running out on 11 November; two arrive after the restart. The two Meridian West approvals end 30 November; the two Riverbend streams dropped under 15% when the Illinois fee rose on 1 November.

sections.heading: Options
sections.body:
Re-route nine shipments to Granger and one to Northstar, hold two on the pad, bring the overflow home, bill the fee (preferred)
Walt Brennan confirms the Granger slots for weeks 45 and 46, Hector Ruiz books the trucks from Thursday, Jenna Fairbanks holds the two loads whose clocks reach 15 November, Carla Dimitriou moves the two Meridian West profiles to Granger, and the account managers bill the Illinois fee on the next Riverbend invoices under clause 9.2.
Extra cost: $60.9k less $23.9k · Positions covered: all 18 · Ten-day clocks: all kept · Third-party: 1 load
Trade-off: Granger runs close to its organic-liquids headroom for two weeks, and the two held loads depend on the kiln being back on 15 November as estimated.

Send everything stranded to third-party outlets
Leave Granger's bookings as they are and send the stranded shipments to Northstar Thermal and Meridian West at their outlet cost.
Cost: $241.9k · Cannot go: 8 shipments · Negative margin: 6 shipments · Meridian West: expires 30 November
Trade-off: Keeps Granger's headroom, but the aqueous loads with a destruction requirement have no outlet outside the network, six shipments go negative, and Meridian West's approvals end this month.

Ask the generators to hold their shipments until 16 November
Hold every inbound load at the generator or on the pad until the kiln is back; nothing moves.
Revenue deferred: $0.71M · Clocks breached: 6 · Cost: $0 · Customers: two with pickup windows
Trade-off: Costs nothing in haul, but breaches six ten-day clocks at Galena Shores, defers the revenue, and two generators have contractual pickup windows this week.

sections.body:
Each shipment with its new destination, tons, the extra cost on the rate card and the date it must leave.

Goal: Keep every accepted stream with a permitted outlet that has capacity when it arrives, and every stream above the margin floor, across the 13 facilities and the third-party outlets. Check each nightly load of profiles, manifests, bookings, outlet approvals and the price book; when a shipment loses its outlet, an approval runs out or a stream falls under the floor, size it, look at what the rest of the network can take, and come back with what can still be done.
Decision asked: Confirm the re-routes, the holds and the outlet loads so every stranded shipment has an outlet inside its clock, and bill the fee on the streams under the floor
Deadline: Granger slots confirmed before the trucks are booked on Wednesday 4 November at noon; the first clock runs out on 11 November; the kiln is back on feed on 15 November

sections.heading: Re-routes inside the network
sections.body:
4. Covering every position costs $60.9k of extra haul and outlet cost, less $23.9k saved on the overflow streams; the kiln costs $96,000 a day while it is down.
Nine re-routes to Granger on the rate card, one to Northstar Thermal, two holds and two keeps at no cost, two overflow streams home at a saving, two fee pass-throughs. Sending everything stranded to outlets instead costs $241.9k and leaves eight shipments with no outlet that meets their requirement.

fromGoal.title: Halden Biopharma proposal: six streams, three years, for Priya by Friday

sections.heading: S-1 Contract summary
sections.body:
Quote on Granger for the QR-14 streams, with Port Terrell as the alternative when its first-quarter plan is published.
Process water, solvent, lab packs and product-contact solids incinerated at Granger at the book; aerosols at Cypress Landing; scrubber water to Bayou Verde deep well. Port Terrell named as the alternative in the schedule, to move at the first contract review once its plan shows room. Close the EPA identification number before 1 January.
Quote a year: $3.56M
Margin: $1.24M · 34.7%
Capacity: in the bookings
Approval: VP Sales and Director

sections.heading: S-3 Price and full cost by stream
sections.body:
3. On the Granger routing the quote is $3.56M a year at 34.7% margin on full cost, above the floor, with no stream under 15%.
The process water earns 35.9% at $740.00 a ton carrying the 1,020-mile haul; the solvent is the lowest stream at 25.0%; the scrubber water on deep well the highest. Quoted on Port Terrell the margin would be 43.0%, on capacity that is not confirmed. Deep well for the process water is the cheapest route and is ruled out by QR-14.

sections.heading: Open items
sections.body:
• Port Terrell has not published its first-quarter 2027 plan; the alternative is stated in the schedule and the stream moves there at the first contract review if the plan shows room.
• Halden's EPA identification number is applied for and not issued; no manifest moves until it is, whatever the contract date.
• Tidewater's permit renewal decision is due 18 December; the solvent is not quoted there, so nothing in the quote rests on it.
